We will deal with a modified conceptual model, which is below. Download this graphics file and insert it into your Quarto notebook.

Hypotheses:
Impact of External Factors on Attitudes towards Behavior

Impact of Demographics.  

H1a:       Consumers’ age will be negatively related to attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

H1b:      Consumers’ education will be positively related to attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

H1c:       Consumers’ income will be positively related to attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.     

Impact of Psychographics.

H1d:      Consumers’ need for cognition will be positively related to attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

H1e:       Consumers’ civic consciousness will be positively related to attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

Impact of Social Influences.

H1f:       Consumers’ social community engagement will be positively related to their attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

H1g:       Consumers’ subjective norm will be positively related to their attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

 

Mediating Role of Civic Conscientiousness

H2a:       Consumers’ need for cognition will be positively related to their civic consciousness.

H2b:       Consumers’ social community engagement will be positively related to their civic consciousness.*

H3:         Consumers’ civic consciousness will mediate the impact of (a) the need for cognition and (b) social community engagement on the attitudes towards buying the brands that use realistic ads.

 

Factors that Affect Perceived Subjective Norm

H4a: Consumers’ civic consciousness will be positively related to subjective norm.

H4b: Consumers’ online community engagement will be positively related to subjective norm.

 

Factors that Affect Perceived Behavioral Control

H5a: Consumers’ age will be negatively related to perceived behavioral control.

H5b: Consumers’ education will be positively related to perceived behavioral control.

H5c: Consumers’ income will be positively related to perceived behavioral control.

 

Determinants of Behavioral Intentions

Impact of attitudes towards behavior on Behavioral Intention

 H6: Consumers’ attitudes towards buying from the brands that use realistic ads will be positively related to their intention to buy from the brands that use realistic ads.

 Impact of Subjective Norm on Behavioral Intention

 H7: Consumers’ subjective norm will be positively related to their intention to buy from the brands that use realistic ads.

 Impact of perceived behavioral control on Behavioral Intention

H8: Consumers’ perceived behavioral control will be positively related to the intention to buy from the brands that use realistic ads.

 

Moderators

Age.

H9a: Consumers’ age will moderate the relationships depicted in H1g (the positive impact of subjective norms on attitudes), such that the relationship will be stronger with increasing age.

H9b: Consumers’ age will moderate the relationships depicted in H7 (the positive impact of subjective norms on intentions), such that the relationship will be stronger with increasing age

Civic Consciousness.

H10a: Consumers’ civic consciousness will moderate the relationships depicted in H1g (the positive impact of subjective norms on purchase attitudes), such that the relationship will be weaker with increasing civic consciousness.

H10b: Consumers’ civic consciousness will moderate the relationships depicted in H6 (the positive impact of subjective norm on purchase intentions), such that the relationship will be weaker with increasing civic consciousness.
